issues.title: Color swatches lack visible labels and selection state

quote.text: Trying to see if this first color dot is blue

issues.why: All five users repeatedly clicked unlabeled color swatches (element 7) trying to find blue, but the swatches show no text labels, no hover/focus indication, and no selected state. Users could not identify which swatch represented blue nor confirm a selection, causing repeated trial-and-error clicks and eventual abandonment.

fix.summary: Add visible text labels to each color swatch and a clear selected state indicator.
fix.before: Color swatches are icon-only buttons with no accessible name, no visible label, and no visual selected state.
fix.after: .color-swatch { position: relative; } .color-swatch::after { content: attr(data-color-name); position: absolute; bottom: -1.5em; left: 50%; transform: translateX(-50%); white-space: nowrap; font-size: 0.75rem; color: #333; } .color-swatch[aria-pressed="true"] { outline: 3px solid #0066cc; outline-offset: 2px; }

issues.title: Checkout page missing; users land on product homepage

quote.text: Let me check out the Everyday Tee first - that sounds like what I'm looking for

issues.why: The URL path '/checkout/' serves a product homepage (S1) with no cart, checkout form, or payment controls. Users must first navigate to a product page (S2), select options, add to bag, then find a separate checkout flow. None reached payment.

fix.summary: Route '/checkout/' to a checkout flow with cart summary and payment, or rename the URL to match the product listing page.
fix.before: Current flow: /checkout/ -> product homepage (S1) -> product page (S2) -> add to bag -> unknown cart -> unknown checkout.
fix.after: Expected flow: /checkout/ -> cart review -> shipping -> payment -> confirmation. If the page is a product listing, change the URL to '/shop/' or '/products/'.

issues.title: Size buttons lack visible selected state

quote.text: Medium size selected, quick and easy.

issues.why: Users clicked 'M' (element 20) but received no visual confirmation that Medium was selected. Diego clicked M twice (steps 4 and 6), Ana clicked M then later doubted selection, Zahara scrolled up/down to verify. The absence of a selected state forces users to guess or re-click.

fix.summary: Add a clear selected state style to size buttons.
fix.before: Size buttons (XS, S, M, L, XL, XXL) show no visual difference when selected.
fix.after: .size-button[aria-pressed="true"] { background-color: #000; color: #fff; border-color: #000; } .size-button:focus-visible { outline: 3px solid #0066cc; outline-offset: 2px; }

issues.title: Color swatches and navigation buttons have no accessible names

quote.text: Trying to see if this first color dot is blue

issues.why: Element 7 (color swatch) and header icon buttons (elements 7, 8, 9) have empty accessible names. Screen readers announce only 'button'. Kwame (non-native English reader) and Elaine (lower digital confidence) cannot rely on visual cues alone. This violates WCAG 4.1.2 and blocks non-visual users from identifying controls.

fix.summary: Provide accessible names for each color swatch and icon-only navigation button.
fix.after: <button class="color-swatch" aria-label="Select Blue"></button> and <button aria-label="Open menu"><svg>...</svg></button>

issues.title: Touch targets smaller than 40x40 px on mobile

quote.text: Looking for the blue color option among those small dots

issues.why: Zahara (mobile-only) struggled to tap the small color swatches (element 3 on S2, element 7 on S3). Expert findings measure tap targets at 34x34 px, below the 40x40 px minimum (WCAG 2.5.8). This caused mis-taps and difficulty selecting blue on mobile.

fix.summary: Increase tap target size for color swatches and navigation controls to at least 40x40 px.

issues.alt: I notice the product page for The Everyday Tee. I need to find the blue color option and select medium size before adding to bag. The color dots are small and might be hard to tap accurately on my phone.

issues.title: Low contrast text on navigation and size labels

quote.text: Trying to find the blue color selection

issues.why: Navigation text ('Shop', 'Tees') and size label 'XXL' measure 3.2:1 contrast, below the 4.5:1 AA requirement (WCAG 1.4.3). Elaine (68, lower digital confidence) and Kwame (non-native reader) may struggle to read these labels, adding cognitive load during an already confusing task.

fix.summary: Increase text contrast to at least 4.5:1 for navigation and size labels.

expert.finding: The blue t-shirt image has a row of five color swatches with no visible selection state, so users cannot confirm they have chosen blue before adding to cart.
expert.suggestion: Add a clear visual indicator (border or highlight) to the selected blue swatch and label it 'Blue'.

expert.finding: The color swatches (Bone, Black, Grey, Blue, Green) and size buttons (XS, S, M, L, XL, XXL) show no visible selected state, so users cannot confirm they have chosen blue and Medium before adding to bag.
expert.suggestion: Add a clear visual indicator (such as a border or highlight) to the selected color and size buttons.

expert.finding: The XXL size button is disabled with no explanation, which may confuse users and prevent them from understanding size availability.
expert.suggestion: Remove the disabled XXL button or replace it with an unavailable state accompanied by a tooltip or message explaining why it cannot be selected.
